Revised Python code to look for inline price arrays in script tags and extract possible price series:
# filename: cardmarket_scrape_js.py
import requests
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
import re

urls = {
    'Oko, Thief of Crowns': 'https://www.cardmarket.com/en/Magic/Products/Singles/Throne-of-Eldraine/Oko-Thief-of-Crowns',
    'Once Upon a Time': 'https://www.cardmarket.com/en/Magic/Products/Singles/Throne-of-Eldraine/Once-Upon-a-Time',
    'Veil of Summer': 'https://www.cardmarket.com/en/Magic/Products/Singles/Core-2020/Veil-of-Summer'
}

def get_price_series(url):
    r = requests.get(url, timeout=20)
    soup = BeautifulSoup(r.text, 'html.parser')
    series = []
    for s in soup.find_all('script'):
        text = s.get_text()
        # Attempt to find arrays like [12.34, 11.98, ...]
        matches = re.findall(r"\[(?:\s*\d+\.\d+\s*,?\s*)+\]", text)
        for m in matches:
            vals = re.findall(r"\d+\.\d+", m)
            series.extend([float(v) for v in vals if 0 < float(v) < 1000])
    if series:
        return max(series), min(series)
    return None, None

for name, url in urls.items():
    hi, lo = get_price_series(url)
    print(f"{name}: high={hi}, low={lo}")
